parts.text:
DEMO_PR_URL: https://github.com/olgaiv39/pr-integrity-demo/pull/2
Use this URL for every authoring-time preview.

ROLE AND GOAL
Build "PR Integrity Review": one reviewer, one GitHub pull request. Fetch evidence, compute six
deterministic signals in plain JavaScript, show the reviewer where to look before reading the
diff. Never judge code quality, guess who wrote a change, claim a defect, or mention AI
authorship. Scaffold in one pass: no restatement, no alternatives, no code explanation unless
validation fails.

AUTHORING SEQUENCE
1 Inspect the available read-only GitHub tool schemas. No other server, no write tool, no
  commits, trees, issues, other pull requests, review state or search.
2 Select the smallest exact tool set covering E1, E2, E3.
3 Call scaffold_app once with the app name, description and those tools. Take the appId and
  keep the default starter temporarily — preview_app_tool needs an existing appId and an
  already-assigned tool, so no preview can happen before this.
4 Persist this specification with refine_app. Ask no product questions, propose no alternative
  design, restate nothing.
5 Preview every required assigned tool against DEMO_PR_URL. Target three preview_app_tool
  calls, one per capability; a fourth only if the schemas prove E3 needs two distinct tools,
  such as separate check-run and commit-status capabilities. Four is the maximum, every call
  needs my approval, and the fourth is not for experimentation, repeated output or an
  unverified fallback. If more than four would be needed, stop and report the mismatch.
6 Inspect the real outputs and write field accessors against them; never invent a tool name,
  argument, field or response shape. Where E3 is split, write one parser per confirmed raw
  response — never one shared raw schema.
7 Build the complete app with edit_app: one self-contained HTML document — no CDN asset,
  external font, import, framework or icon library. window.archestra is injected; do not
  bootstrap the SDK or wire postMessage. No archestra.llm.complete, fetch, XMLHttpRequest or
  WebSocket.
8 Render and run validate_app; fix only concrete diagnostics.
Report a blocker instead of improvising if a capability is absent, a preview lacks required
evidence, patch text or CI results cannot be read, a parser is unsafe to write, or the
work needs a runtime LLM, a second MCP server, network access or a write. Name the blocked
capability, the stage, the affected signals, and whether the rest can still be scaffolded.

MCP CAPABILITIES
E1 one pull request: title, body, author, state, draft flag, base and head ref, head SHA,
   changed-file count, additions, deletions, and a web URL only if the response carries one.
E2 files changed: filename, status (added/modified/removed/renamed), additions, deletions,
   unified-diff patch text where returned.
E3 CI for the head SHA: check runs and/or commit statuses with name, status, conclusion.
Report the tool bound to each capability and any missing; never substitute. At runtime call
archestra.tools.list() only to confirm they exist, never to rediscover identities.

APP WORKFLOW
Input: owner, repo, number, or a pasted pull-request URL split locally by regex, plus one
primary "Load pull request" button. On submit call E1, then E2, then E3, never paginating. E1
and E2 are one bound call each; E3 is one, or two only if the confirmed schemas require separate
check-run and commit-status tools. With two, parse each raw response with its own accessor,
normalize each to { name, state, conclusion }, merge the normalized records, drop exact
duplicates, and evaluate validation-evidence over the merged list. If one E3 tool succeeds and
the other fails or is incomplete, keep any observed attention evidence, else report
validation-evidence inconclusive; Retry re-runs only the failed bound tool. Render E1 as it
lands, then compute every signal in the browser: no further calls, no Cancel or timeout.

DATA AND LIMITS
Caps: 100 changed files analyzed; 100 reviewable patches parsed; 200000 characters per patch;
1000000 characters of patch text total; 30 evidence rows per signal, with "showing N of M";
2000-character note.
File classification, first match wins:
1 lockfile: package-lock.json, npm-shrinkwrap.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, bun.lockb,
  poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, go.sum, mix.lock,
  pubspec.lock, packages.lock.json, gradle.lockfile
2 manifest: package.json, requirements*.txt, Pipfile, pyproject.toml, setup.py, go.mod,
  Cargo.toml, Gemfile, composer.json, pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), libs.versions.toml, mix.exs,
  pubspec.yaml, *.csproj
3 generated: under dist/ build/ out/ target/ vendor/ node_modules/ coverage/ __snapshots__/
  .next/ .nuxt/ generated/, plus *.min.js, *.min.css, *.snap, *.pb.go, *_pb2.py
4 coverage config: jest.config.*, karma.conf.js, .nycrc, codecov.yml, tox.ini,
  sonar-project.properties, .coveragerc
5 test: under tests/ test/ spec/ specs/ __tests__/ e2e/ integration-tests/, or name matching
  [.\-_](test|spec)\.<ext>, test_*.py, *_test.go, *Test.java/kt/cs
6 CI config: .github/workflows/**, .gitlab-ci.yml, azure-pipelines.yml, Jenkinsfile,
  .circleci/config.yml
7 docs: *.md, *.mdx, *.rst, *.txt, *.adoc, or under docs/
8 production source: everything else
"Reviewable" excludes classes 1 and 3.

DETERMINISTIC SIGNALS
Status attention, clear or inconclusive; priority high, medium or low. No score or percentage.

task-context — Task context is thin or unlinked.
thin = body under 120 characters after stripping HTML comments and collapsing whitespace.
unlinked = no #123, no closes/fixes/resolves/refs #123, no github.com issue URL.
attention if thin or unlinked, except a not-thin body under an "Acceptance criteria",
"Requirements", "Scope", "Goal" or "Context" heading, which is not flagged unlinked. high if thin
and unlinked and additions+deletions >= 200.

scope-spread — Change scope is broad or scattered.
Over reviewable files with changes: attention if files >= 12, or distinct first path segments >= 4
(root files count as "<root>"), or changed lines >= 500. high if two or more cross. Always show:
each measurement against its threshold, a per-directory breakdown, the five largest files, the
count excluded as lockfile or generated.

test-coverage-balance — Behavior changed without a test change.
prodChanged = observed class-8 files added or modified with changed lines; testTouched =
observed class-5 files added or modified with additions. attention if the file list is complete
and prodChanged is non-empty and testTouched is empty; clear if testTouched is non-empty, or the
list is complete and prodChanged is empty; inconclusive if the list is incomplete and
testTouched is empty. high if attention with production changed lines >= 100, else medium.
Ignore renames with no additions or deletions. File metadata only — patch caps are irrelevant.

test-weakening — Possible test weakening.
Scan class-5 patches, class-4 for (e). attention if any sub-check matches; show the matched
patch lines.
  a class-5 file with status removed — high
  b removed lines matching ^-\s*(it|test|describe|context|bench)\s*(\.\w+)?\s*\( or
    ^-\s*(async\s+)?def\s+test_\w+ or ^-\s*func\s+(Test|Benchmark|Fuzz)\w+\s*\( or
    ^-\s*(@Test\b|(public\s+)?void\s+test\w*\s*\(), when removed minus added >= 2 — medium
  c added skip marker: it/test/describe/context .skip/.todo/.failing, xit(, xdescribe(, @skip,
    @unittest.skip, @pytest.mark.(skip|skipif|xfail), t.Skip(, @Disabled, @Ignore,
    testing.Short() — high
  d + and - lines starting with expect, assert, assertXxx, should, chai., sinon.assert, verify,
    require.<x>, or containing .toBe/.toEqual/.toThrow/.toHaveBeenCalled, when removed minus
    added >= 3 — medium
  e in class-4 files, key=number pairs off + and - lines for statements, branches, functions,
    lines, global, threshold, minimum_coverage, fail_under, target; match when an added value is
    lower than the removed value for that key — high
clear only when every changed class-4 and class-5 file had usable patch text and none matched —
including the trivial case where none changed. Otherwise inconclusive, never clear.

dependency-surface — Dependency surface changed.
attention if any class-1 or class-2 file changed. From class-2 patch text only, extract
candidate entries: JSON "name": "version" pairs, requirements.txt name+specifier lines, go.mod
name+vNNN lines, TOML name = lines, Gemfile gem 'name'. On + only = added, - only = removed,
both = version-changed. "Candidate" because the JSON pattern also matches unrelated fields. Never
parse lockfiles. high if a lockfile changed while its sibling manifest did not, or if an entry was
added and the body matches none of
depend/dependency/dependencies/package/library/upgrade/bump/version/lockfile. Compare lockfile
against manifest changed lines.

validation-evidence — Validation evidence missing, pending, or failed.
Normalize E3 into name/state/conclusion for the head SHA. attention if: no checks at all
(medium); any conclusion is failure, timed_out, action_required, error or stale (high); any
state is queued, in_progress, pending, waiting or requested (medium); or checks exist, none
failed or pending, and no name matches test|spec|ci|build|check|verify|lint|e2e|unit|
integration|pytest|jest|gradle|maven|tox (medium). cancelled, neutral and skipped are evidence
only. Show the short head SHA, the check table, the draft flag.

Order: attention (high, medium, low), then inconclusive, then clear; within a group as listed.

INCOMPLETE-DATA RULE
Input is incomplete when a cap was hit, fewer files arrived than E1 reported, a needed patch was
absent, or a stage was denied. Then, everywhere:
- Positive evidence survives: a signal that already matched stays attention at the highest
  priority actually demonstrated, labels its coverage partial or limited, and names what was not
  read. Incompleteness alone never raises a priority.
- Missing data blocks clear: if nothing matched but unseen input could change the result, the
  status is inconclusive, never clear.
By signal: task-context unaffected (E1 only); scope-spread attention on any crossed threshold,
else inconclusive; test-coverage-balance clear once a qualifying test change was observed, else
inconclusive, its attention condition being an absence; test-weakening inconclusive if nothing
matched and any changed class-4/5 file went unread or may be missing from the list;
dependency-surface attention on file metadata alone; validation-evidence inconclusive if E3 was
denied, unavailable or incomplete and nothing matched — never "no checks" then.
Review confidence is a separate page badge measuring E1/E2 changed-file and patch coverage only
— E3 denial or incompleteness affects validation-evidence but never the badge: full = complete
file list, every reviewable file had patch text; partial = complete list, some had none, list
them; limited = a cap was hit or fewer files arrived than reported, name the cap and the count
unanalyzed.

INTERFACE AND DESIGN
One reviewer workspace, one scrolling column: header, input, progress, summary, six cards,
decision panel. Developer-tool look — compact, evidence-first, high contrast, system fonts,
subtle borders, modest radius, restrained status colours always with a text label. No hero, nav,
gradient, glassmorphism, heavy shadow, chart, gauge, mascot, oversized card, or animation beyond
small loading and disclosure transitions. Inline SVG only where it aids scanning.
Use Archestra's injected baseline stylesheet, theme variables and suitable .arch-* components
for cards, buttons, inputs, badges and loading indicators. Write only app-specific CSS; do not
recreate a complete theme.
Header: "PR Integrity Review" and a one-line purpose.
Input: labelled owner, repo, number fields with examples — one row wide, stacked narrow — plus
the Load button. After E1 show title, state, author, short head SHA, additions, deletions and
file count as secondary text; link to the pull request only if E1 supplied a URL.
Progress: E1, E2, E3 as three named stages, no percentages. Summary: confidence badge, counts of
attention, clear and inconclusive, one sentence explaining partial or limited.
Cards: six in order, status legible before reading, compact by default, each with title, status,
priority, short reason, measured evidence, coverage label. Evidence and verification expand in
place — never a modal — keyboard-operable. Paths, check names, SHAs and patch lines in
monospace, wrapped or truncated safely. Keep observed evidence separate from reviewer guidance,
state the false-positive boundary briefly, end each attention card with a question for the
author. Two columns wide only if evidence stays scannable; one column below.
Decision panel: separated, after the findings. Ready for focused review, Changes requested,
Needs deeper validation, Accepted risk; optional note with a live counter; explicit Save, then
its timestamp. Nothing saves automatically.
Accessibility: semantic headings and landmarks, visible labels, visible keyboard focus, live
status for loading and errors, meaning never by colour alone, buttons disabled only when the
action cannot run, no horizontal scroll at desktop width, no modal in the main flow.

STATES AND ERRORS
initial: input plus one paragraph on what is checked, no empty cards. loading: per-stage
progress, input disabled. auth-required: a call rejects with { code: "auth_required", url } —
render url as a link, plus Retry. not-found: show the exact owner/repo/number tried, keep the
entered values. forbidden: name the failing capability; if only E3 failed, continue with
validation-evidence inconclusive. partial and limited: render all available data with the badge
and its reason. empty: all six clear — say so, still list all six measured values, decision panel
available. success: normal results. tool-error: plain message, raw error code collapsed, Retry
re-runs only the failed stage and keeps stages that already succeeded.

STORAGE
Persist only the decision, in archestra.storage.user, key decision:<owner>__<repo>__<number>,
value { decision, note, headSha, savedAt, signalsAtSave }, signalsAtSave listing the ids that
were attention. Restore by direct get() for the same pull request, with its timestamp. If the
head SHA differs from the stored one, mark it stale and show both; never overwrite or delete
automatically. Never list another key, use archestra.storage.shared, or persist pull-request
content.

NON-GOALS
No repository picker, list of pull requests, multi-repo view, pagination, chart, setting,
export, theme, second integration, GitHub write, runtime LLM, composite score, or seventh signal.

COST BOUNDARY
Call refine_app exactly once. Call edit_app once for the initial complete build. Run validate_app
once, then allow at most one additional edit_app call to repair concrete diagnostics and one final
validate_app call. Never regenerate the complete app after validation. Do not restate tool schemas,
preview payloads, generated HTML or this specification in chat. If another repair pass would be
required, stop and report the remaining diagnostics.

VALIDATION AND REPORT
Run validate_app, fix concrete failures, then report in under 200 words: the tool bound to each
of E1, E2 and E3; any missing capability; whether E2 returns patch text; whether E3 is
available; how many files E2 returned against E1's count; remaining diagnostics; anything you
could not implement.
Now previewing the assigned tool's methods against the demo PR (owner: `olgaiv39`, repo: `pr-integrity-demo`, number: `2`) to confirm real response shapes before writing parsers.
Now the render functions for PR summary, summary bar, cards, and decision panel:
Now let's assemble the final HTML by replacing the placeholder script block with the full logic, then validate with node/basic syntax check before uploading.
Syntax is valid. Now let's do a quick logic sanity test against the actual preview data before wiring it into the app.
All six signals compute correctly against the real preview data. Now let's push this into the app via `edit_app` using `replacementHtmlSource`.
Clean on both static checks and live render. Per the cost boundary, that's the single validation pass — no further edit/validate cycle needed.

**[PR Integrity Review](/a/pr-integrity-review)**

Enter an owner/repo/number (or paste a PR URL) and click "Load pull request" to review one PR at a time before reading its diff.

**Tool binding**: all three capabilities are covered by one assigned GitHub tool, `github__pull_request_read`, called with different `method` values — E1: `method: "get"`, E2: `method: "get_files"`, E3: `method: "get_check_runs"` + `method: "get_status"` (two distinct bound calls, each with its own accessor since check-runs and commit-status are different response shapes). No capability was missing.

- E2 returns unified-diff patch text on every changed file (confirmed against the demo PR).
- E3 is available: check-runs return `name/status/conclusion`; commit-status returns `state` (with an empty `statuses` array in this PR, since combined status is "pending" with 0 sub-statuses) — the app normalizes and merges both.
- Against the demo PR, E1 reported 12 changed files and E2 returned all 12.
- Static validation and the live render are both clean — no diagnostics to fix.
- Nothing was unimplementable: all six signals, the caps, the state machine (auth-required/forbidden/partial/limited/empty/tool-error with per-stage retry), and the storage-only decision record are wired per spec.

enhancement.description: Six deterministic checks (files, diff patches, check-runs, commit status) for a single GitHub PR — where to look before you read the diff.
enhancement.prompt: Build me a tool that lets me review one GitHub pull request at a time by pasting its URL, pulling the PR details, file diffs, and check-run/commit-status results to compute six deterministic risk signals before I read the code, and showing me exactly where to look without judging code quality or guessing authorship.
enhancement.response:
Built — **PR Integrity Review** is live and ready to use on a single GitHub pull request at a time.

- Loads a PR by owner/repo/number or a pasted URL, pulling metadata, changed files, check runs, and commit status through `github__pull_request_read`.
- Computes six deterministic signals in plain JavaScript from the diff/patch data and the merged check-run + commit-status results — no guessing at code quality or authorship.
- Normalizes and merges two distinct response shapes for CI state: check-runs (`name/status/conclusion`) and commit status (`state` + `statuses`), each with its own parser since they're structurally different.
- Renders a summary bar, signal cards, and a decision panel that points you to what's worth reviewing closely before you open the diff.
- Handles every real-world state cleanly — auth-required, forbidden, partial, limited, empty, and tool-error — each with its own retry path.
- Keeps a storage-only decision record so your review call on a PR persists locally without any write access back to GitHub.

To use it: enter an owner/repo/number or paste a PR URL, hit "Load pull request," and read the signals before you dive into the diff.
